typed: Explain how a VPN works in simple words

expect: one reply, no duplicate bubbles, sensible tone and casing
lastReply:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet. Everything you send goes through it in scrambled form, so nobody in between can read it.

Here is how it goes:

Your device scrambles (encrypts) your data and sends it to the VPN company's machine.
That machine unscrambles it and talks to the website for you.
The website sees the VPN's address instead of yours, so your location looks different.
The reply comes back the same way, scrambled again on the last leg.

It helps on public Wi-Fi, since strangers on the same network can't read your traffic. It also hides what you browse from your internet provider. It does not make you anonymous: the VPN company can see your activity, and sites can still know you by your logins.
